title: Real-Time In-Situ Insights: Dynamic Mapping with 4D STEM
content: In the past decade, the family of techniques commonly known as 4D STEM has grown from a unique capability available only to a few labs worldwide [1] into a seemingly ubiquitous one, with hundreds of publications each year utilizing 4D STEM results. Much of the value of 4D STEM lies in its flexibility, allowing a wealth of acquired data to be mined for months or years after the experimental work is completed. However, the volume of data produced can also be a liability. If processing and analyzing a single dataset takes hours, it becomes difficult to quickly determine at the microscope whether the data captured the desired structure or dynamics. The volume of data, and thus the effort required to rapidly discern whether it is good, increases even further if the experiment is an in-situ one and the dataset includes the fifth dimension of time. This is particularly detrimental for in-situ since the experiments often require rapid data processing to make real-time decisions based on sample dynamics. If changes are not discernible from the live view, it hinders informed decision-making and reduces the chances of collecting valuable data.
